newsitem.title: THAILAND: Krungthai Thanakit sees 1996 net growth.
newsitem.headline: Krungthai Thanakit sees 1996 net growth.

text.p: Krungthai Thanakit Plc president Phirasilp Subhapholsiri said on Wednesday the company should report a profit between 1.1 billion and 1.2 billion baht ($44-48 million) in 1996.
This would represent a 25 to 30 percent increase over the 901.73 million baht profit the bank reported in 1995.

"I think the third quarter is favourable compared to the output of the industry this year," Phirasilp told Reuters in an interview. "We did very well in the first half and it's still looking pretty good on a year-to-year basis."

Phirasilp said new securities partner Barclays de Zoete Wedd was taking about two percent of total market share and passing it to Krungthai Thanakit. The contribution brings Krungthai Thanakit's market share of securities trading to around four percent but Phirasilp said he expected it to rise further.
He said he expected the company to maintain its 65-35 percent revenue split between finance and securities operations and to continue with its cautious lending policy.
Krungthai Thanakit shares were up 2.50 baht at 70.50 in late afternoon trade.
